feedback: This is iteration 0, so there is no race evidence yet. The controller uses the antisymmetric weights (-1.0 to +1.0) that the geometry implies, a moderate kp of 3.0, and last_direction line-loss recovery. The main integration concerns I expect to address from the first race are: (a) whether the 12 mm spacing across 48 mm total span keeps the reading sum above 0.05 on the tightest bends, since no line-loss data exists yet; (b) whether the 30 mm forward offset gives enough lead for a 1.5 m/s base speed without overshoot on the s-bend and slalom; and (c) whether the 0.12 m wheel track at 0.8 kg limits turn rate on the slalom. If the next race shows line-loss events on the slalom or s-bend, widen the sensor span before changing the forward offset. If it shows oscillation with no line loss, the forward offset or wheel track is the more likely lever. If completion is reached on all three tracks with low rms_error, keep the layout and only tune the controller.
requested_changes: If the next race shows line_loss_events above zero on the s-bend or slalom, try sensor_positions with x spanning +/-0.032 m (five sensors at 16 mm spacing) to widen the tape-detection footprint; this is the iteration-0 hypothesis (1) and has no race evidence yet.
If the next race shows steering_oscillation or max_error high on the oval with no line loss, try a forward sensor offset of y = 0.05 m (hypothesis 2) to add phase lead and damping.
If the next race shows completion but completion_time above 2 s, try mass 0.6 kg with wheel_track 0.10 m (hypotheses 3 and 4) to increase slalom turn agility and acceleration, and watch for slip.
